rounds.fact: Star ratings lasted until 2010. They were retired because almost everyone rated either 5 stars or 1, so the site switched to thumbs up/down.
Craigslist's design has barely changed since the 1990s, on purpose. The founder has said repeatedly that plain text links serve the function better than a redesign would.
Wikipedia's interface has stayed remarkably close to its original look for two decades. The visual restraint was intentional, to keep the focus on editing and content rather than design.
LinkedIn launched in 2003 out of a founder's living room. By 2005 it was already leaning into the dense, spreadsheet-like profile layout that professional networking sites still use.
eBay started in 1995 as AuctionWeb, reportedly built to help the founder's fiancee trade Pez dispensers. By 1999 it was already a sprawling grid of category links and live auctions.
